svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A sodium atom (2,8,1) and a chlorine atom (2,8,7)."], [1.5, "Sodium transfers its outer electron to chlorine."], [3.5, "Both now have full outer shells: Na\u207a (2,8) and Cl\u207b (2,8,8). The oppositely charged ions attract: ionic bonding."], [6, "In sodium chloride, ions build up into a giant ionic lattice."], [10, "Each Na\u207a is surrounded by 6 Cl\u207b and each Cl\u207b by 6 Na\u207a. The ratio is 1 : 1, so the formula is NaCl."]]
svg.title: Sodium chloride: ionic bonding and the lattice
svg.desc: Electron transfer from sodium to chlorine to form Na⁺ and Cl⁻, then a giant ionic lattice of sodium chloride in which each ion is surrounded by six of the opposite charge.
svg.text: Sodium chloride: ionic bonding and the giant ionic lattice
Left: dot-and-cross diagram. Right: part of the lattice (purple: Na⁺, green: Cl⁻).

g.data-info: Na (2,8,1) loses its one outer electron to become Na⁺ (2,8): a full outer shell.
Cl (2,8,7) gains one electron to become Cl⁻ (2,8,8): a full outer shell.
Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, acting in all directions. Lots of energy is needed to break it: melting point 801 °C.
Millions of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a regular cubic arrangement. Each ion is surrounded by 6 ions of the opposite charge.

g.text: each ion: 6 neighbours of opposite charge
